title: Applying Held Deposits at the Final Bill — Good Faith & Price Estimates
content:
All deposits held on one Good Faith & Price Estimates estimate are combined when the rendered service is billed, which is at the final bill on every estimate type. Each deposit collection is applied to the linked hospital account, oldest collection first, until the account's patient balance after the package or uninsured pricing is covered; whatever remains of the deposits after that is refunded. Deposits are never moved to a different estimate or to an unrelated hospital account.

**One application per collection.** A deposit collection is applied at most once, and what is left of a collection after an application or a retained fee is the only amount that may be refunded from it. Whether a collection has already been applied is read from the estimate's own deposit activity — an application entry names the collection it draws on — not from the patient's account of events.

**What is left of a collection.** For each deposit collection, what remains is its amount less any application, refund or retained fee drawing on that collection.

**Effect on the hospital account.** An application appears on the linked hospital account as a payment of the applied prepayment deposit, carrying the deposit's payment confirmation number, the amount applied and the posting date.

## Worked example (hypothetical figures)

Two collections are held: 300.00 collected first and 200.00 collected later. The account's patient balance after pricing is 400.00.

1. The older collection is applied first: 300.00, leaving 100.00 of the balance uncovered.
2. The later collection covers the remaining 100.00; 100.00 of that collection is left.
3. The 100.00 left of the later collection is refunded; nothing is left of the older collection to refund.

| Collection | Amount | Applied | Left and refunded |
|---|---|---|---|
| older | 300.00 | 300.00 | 0.00 |
| later | 200.00 | 100.00 | 100.00 |
